nodes.title: How to use
widgets_values:
# MiniMax H3 — multi-shot UGC beat

One Run makes **one beat**: a single 12-second clip that may contain several
shots, with native synced audio — voice, room tone and music generated in one
pass. Render beat after beat, then stitch them with the assemble workflow.

## The loop

1. Fill **Casting** and **Music bed** once — who the person is, what the
   product is, what the room is, what the score does. You never retype these.
2. Fill **This beat** — summary, retention analysis, shot list, soundscape.
3. Run. You get `beat_00001_.mp4` and `lastframe_00001_.png`.
4. For beat 2, change only **This beat** and Run again.

## Three prompt boxes, not two

H3 mandates this section order:

    subject_definitions → summary → retention_analysis →
    detailed_description → overall_soundscape → non_diegetic_music

The set-once sections are the 1st, 3rd and 6th, the per-beat ones the 2nd, 4th
and 5th — they interleave, so a single "casting + beat" join would emit them out
of order. Three boxes joined top to bottom keep the order H3 wants.
**Never delete the first line of a box** — that line is the section label.

Aim for **350–500 words across the three boxes**. An under-written prompt is
the single most common cause of identity drift.

**retention_analysis** is the identity lever, one line per subject:

    <Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 2]): fully_preserved - ...
    <Subject 3> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 2]): attribute_transfer - ...

`fully_preserved` means do not change it. `attribute_transfer` means carry the
look across; framing may change. It names which shots each subject appears in,
so it changes with the beat — that is why it sits in **This beat**.

Write every camera move as **motion type + amplitude + speed** ("pushes in with
small amplitude at slow speed"). Write dialogue as `(S1) says: <d>[English]
...</d>`. Write music concretely — *nylon-string guitar, 80 BPM, plucked
eighths, drops 6 dB under the second line* — not "warm", not "uplifting";
`N/A` for no score.

## Two modes, one switch

**mode** on the generator node picks the model:

- **off = Ref2VA** (default) — your reference images, and optionally a
  reference video and a voice clip, feed the model. **Use this for anything
  with dialogue.**
- **on = FL2VA** — first-frame / last-frame interpolation. This mode has **no
  reference-audio path, so it re-rolls the speaker**: the voice changes between
  beats. Use it for action and B-roll only.

The switch is lazy, so only the selected checkpoint is ever loaded. That is why
both 19.5 GB models can ship in one graph.

## Continuity between beats

The **Continuity** group is bypassed. From beat 2 onward select its nodes,
press Ctrl+B to un-bypass, and point `LoadVideo` at your **hero beat** — the
beat whose look every other beat should match.

**Always point it at the hero beat, never at the newest one.** Chaining beat N
from beat N−1 compounds artifacts on every generation; every beat referencing
beat 1 does not.

Un-bypass **Voice lock** and upload 5–10 s of clean speech to pin a voice to a
character. In the prompt, bind it as `<Subject 1> (S1) speaks with the voice in
<Audio 1>.` — far more reliable than inheriting a voice from a reference video.

## Size, length and speed

**megapixels 0.8 at 9:16** gives H3 a 672x1184 portrait canvas, rounded to 32 —
the proven-fast default. **1.0** reaches H3's native cap of 768x1344, the 768 px
short edge. On OOM drop to **0.4 before you shorten the beat**: a shorter beat
costs you a seam, a smaller canvas only costs detail.

**duration 12 s** feeds the frame-grid expression and lands on length 294. H3
tops out around 15 s of useful output. **steps 20**, 24 fps.

`ref_image_size` is **max** (up to a 2048 px short edge) because UGC lives on
face and product-label fidelity. Switch it to **match** for fast drafts.

A 4-step turbo LoRA exists for H3
([drbaph/MiniMax-H3-Turbo-Lora-ComfyUI](https://huggingface.co/drbaph/MiniMax-H3-Turbo-Lora-ComfyUI))
and is **not** installed here. To add it manually: download it into
`models/loras/`, drop a `LoraLoaderModelOnly` between the model switch and the
sampler inside the subgraph, and set `steps` to 8 — about 2.5x faster, at a
real cost in audio quality (at 4 steps the audio path clips outright).

## Outputs

`beat` — the clip. `lastframe` — the final frame as a PNG, written on every
Run with no interaction.

Every image slot ships pointing at the one example photo the launch script
seeds, so the first Queue works with zero uploads. That is the only reason
**First frame** starts there — it is not a meaningful default. Once Run 1 has
written a `lastframe_00001_.png`, pick that from its dropdown before you switch
to FL2VA, and replace `<Picture 2>` with a different angle of the same person
before you un-bypass it.

nodes.title: Model links

## Model links

[Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)

**diffusion_models**

- [minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/diffusion_models/minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors)
- [minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/diffusion_models/minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors)

**text_encoders**

- [qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/text_encoders/qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors)

**vae**

- [minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/vae/minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors)
- [minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/vae/minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors)

## Model storage location

```
ComfyUI/
  models/
    diffusion_models/
      minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors
      minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors
    text_encoders/
      qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors
    vae/
      minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16.safetensors
      minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors
```

Every file above is downloaded by the launch script before ComfyUI starts. It
reads the URLs out of this graph, so a loader without a URL is a missing file.
The optional turbo LoRA is not in this list on purpose — see "How to use".

nodes.title: Casting — set once, never retype
widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> (<Picture 1>, <Picture 2>): Maya, a woman in her late twenties with warm brown skin, dark shoulder-length curls parted on the left, and a small mole under her right eye. She wears an oversized cream ribbed sweater. <Picture 1> is her three-quarter view holding the product, <Picture 2> her straight-on close-up.
<Subject 2> (<Picture 1>): the product, a 50 ml frosted-glass jar with a matte white screw lid and one line of thin black serif type reading "AURELIE".
<Subject 3>: the room, a small apartment bathroom with white subway tile, a round brass-framed mirror, and one window camera-left throwing soft overcast daylight across her face.

nodes.title: This beat — retype every Run
widgets_values:
summary:
Maya sets the jar down on the sink ledge and tells the camera what changed for her skin, then the shot cuts closer as she twists the lid open and shows the texture on her fingertip.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 2]): fully_preserved - face geometry, the mole under the right eye, the curl pattern and hair part, and the cream ribbed sweater carry across both shots unchanged.
<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 2]): fully_preserved - jar proportions, matte white lid and the "AURELIE" label type stay identical, and the label stays legible and correctly spelled at every distance.
<Subject 3> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 2]): attribute_transfer - the tile, mirror and window light of <Picture 1> carry into both shots; the camera position and framing change, the room does not.

detailed_description:
[Shot 1] Medium shot, waist up, <Subject 1> centered with the brass mirror behind her left shoulder. She sets <Subject 2> down on the tile ledge with her right hand, looks into the lens and speaks. The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed across the whole shot. (S1) says: <d>[English] Okay, three weeks in, and I finally have to talk about this one.</d>
[Shot 2] At 00:06.000, the camera cuts to a close-up of her hands and the lower half of her face. She twists the matte white lid off <Subject 2>, tips the jar toward the lens and presses one fingertip into the cream. The camera tilts down with medium amplitude at slow speed to follow her hands, then holds. (S1) says: <d>[English] It is thicker than it looks, you barely need this much.</d>

overall_soundscape:
Close, dry indoor room tone with the faint hum of a bathroom fan. The glass jar sets down on the tile with one short hard tap in [Shot 1]. In [Shot 2] the lid gives a fine gritty twist as it unthreads, and the cream makes a soft wet press under her fingertip. She takes a short audible breath in before her second line.

nodes.title: Music bed — set once
widgets_values:
non_diegetic_music:
A single nylon-string guitar figure at roughly 80 BPM, plucked in steady eighth notes with a soft brushed shaker on the offbeat. It enters under the first line, holds flat through the cut, and drops about 6 dB under the second line.
